meaningMnemonic: This radical is the same as the kanji. It means protect .
This radical is the same as the kanji. It means renew .

A spoon to measure a geoduck is a very approximate measurement. Geoducks are big, spoons are small. Still, we'll get the approximation going, right? Hints Do the comparison. A spoonful of geoduck aka a whole geoduck on a spoon. This is a spoonful, right? This is what the recipe wanted, I think...
readingMnemonic: Maybe this is too much geoduck, even if we're going for an approximate . So, you take the core ( ころ ) of the geoduck and measure that instead. Hints That's a little better. Not too much geoduck. Still a lot, but more like an approximate.

meaningMnemonic: When you leave grain s in your mouth for long enough, they'll turn into flowers of bacteria . These aren't the nice, pretty flowers you'd give your mom on Mother's Day. These are little bacteria flowers that are taking over your mouth. Maybe brush your teeth next time. Hints Imagine how much bacteria would flower in your mouth if you just left grains in there for like, I dunno, a month. That's a lot of nasty bacteria!
readingMnemonic: There is a lot of this bacteria in the Kin g ( きん ) of England's mouth. He eats a lot of grains, and he won't let anyone touch his mouth to clean it, but he refuses to do things himself... so it's absolutely chock full of bacteria. Hints Picture the King's mouth up close. Look at all the bacteria squiggling around and through his teeth and gums. Bleh! Barf!

meaningMnemonic: Something made of gold stand s in a village . It's a bell !  The village bell. Hints Every village has a bell of its own, standing tall and proud and shiny in the middle for everyone to see and hear.
readingMnemonic: The bell rings whenever the Shou gun ( しょう ) arrives in the village. Its ringing echoes throughout the entire village so everyone knows they have to come out and pay their respects. Hints The Shougun bell even sounds like it's warning you that the Shougun has arrived. It makes a loud, low shooooouu shooou sound.

meaningMnemonic: The boat radical and the boat kanji are the same! Hints Boats are boats, you know?
readingMnemonic: The reading is the same reading that you learned with the vocabulary 船 . Hints Since 船 and 舟 both mean "boat", this reading should be pretty easy to remember!

meaningMnemonic: The woman who makes your house a home is your bride . Hints She's in your house because you married her. Thus, she's your bride. Your house is now a home.
readingMnemonic: Now that you have a bride in your house, you can get rid of yo ur mai d ( よめ ), since your bride will do all the cleaning. Hints Your bride is very upset at how sexist you're being right now, and makes you do all the cleaning instead. The maid still gets fired.

meaningMnemonic: Looking up to the cliff , you see the tree s, and the sun shining down on them. Using the sun and the trees (up there on the cliff), you've devised a method to tell what time of the year it is, based on where the shadow from the trees fall. After a while, you develop a bigger system. This system is a whole calendar . Hints Look at the different shadow patterns. Know what they all mean. This is your very own calendar system.
readingMnemonic: Remember the word 歴史 , which means "history"? Using a calendar , you too can remember history (otherwise, who knows when these things happened). So, the reading for this kanji is the same as the reading for 歴史 's beginning, because they're related. Hints Make sure you make the connection between the word 歴史 and this kanji. If you do, it'll be much easier to remember the reading of this kanji.

meaningMnemonic: The sun is being blocked by a rain cloud , making it cloudy . Hints You look up at the sky, trying to find the sun, but it's so cloudy that you can't even find where the sun should be.
readingMnemonic: Remember 雲 ? It means "cloud" and has the same reading as "cloudy," making them both くも . Hints If it's cloudy there are clouds, so if you can read one, you can read the other!

meaningMnemonic: An alligator is considerably dangerous. Considerably terrifying too. Considerably [put your scary adjective here]. Hints The radical meaning and the kanji meaning aren't the same, but we'll get through this together. Just put a considerable amount of effort into this and you'll learn considerably more quickly.
readingMnemonic: Speaking of considerably terrifying, that place known as Nar nia ( なり ) is pretty terrifying. Not sure why children want to go there. Hints Also, things that are "considerably" anything start somewhere. They become ( なり ) whatever "considerable" thing they are now from something smaller before.

meaningMnemonic: You receive instruction in a circle in the dirt . Where are you? Cram school ! Hints Your cram school thinks that you’ll learn better sitting in a circle in the dirt. So there you are in the dirt, receiving your lessons.
readingMnemonic: Not only does your cram school teach kids in a circle in the dirt, it also plays music on a juke box ( じゅく ). Yes, a jukebox. They believe a jukebox's tunes help with cramming. Hints Imagine a jukebox playing loudly right beside you while you’re cramming away. Hard to believe, but the jukebox's melodies do actually amplify the cramming fervor, making you just cram, cram, cram!

meaningMnemonic: From the mouth of your older brother comes... a curse ! Hints Imagine him cursing you. He's not a fan of you, since you are siblings, but to think he'd go so far as to put a curse on you? You can't believe it. What kind of curse did he put upon you?
readingMnemonic: Turns out, he put the no ro ad ( のろ ) curse on you, meaning you can never walk on roads. Hints In your mind, walk around the area where you live. Think about the places you can go that aren't roads. If you try to walk on a road, you can't. This is the no ro ad curse, after all.

meaningMnemonic: After the tsunami the sun comes out again and shines on these spikes . They were super wet before, but you figure the sun probably dried them off. You lean down to touch them and nope, they's still damp . Hints The sun did a little bit of work, so they aren't wet, but they aren't dry either. They're damp.
readingMnemonic: As you're looking at the damp spikes, a shih tzu ( しつ ) prances over, slips on the damp ground, and falls right on the spike! Oh nooo! Hints Luckily the shih tzu is kinda pinned between the spikes, so it isn't dead or anything, but it's definitely stuck. You try to help it out, but you slip because it's so damp and you fall in too! Imagine the sound of your cries mixing in with the shih tzu's as you both struggling to get out but can't because of how damp everything is.

meaningMnemonic: The grain s you have stored in your house reflect on your earnings . If you earn a lot of money, you have more grains. Hints Imagine looking at the grains in the houses of people who make vastly different earnings. The poor artist has only a few sacks of grain. The rich samurai has an extra house just for holding his grain. That's how you know he has much higher earnings than the artist.
readingMnemonic: Another way to check someone's earnings is to see if they have a ca r ( か ). Would someone who doesn't make a lot of money have a car? No! Hints Picture your own earnings. Can you afford a lot of grains and a car?

meaningMnemonic: A sheep with feathers (and presumably wings, too) is able to fly . Hints Imagine the sheep with feathers taking off and flying around. It's an odd sight, but makes sense, kind of.
readingMnemonic: Watching that sheep with feathers and wings flying around made you thirsty. You remember that you have a ca r ke ttle ( かけ ), so you reach into your car and grab your car kettle to make a special car-kettle brew. Hints Imagine yourself enjoying the cozy car-kettle brew, while admiring the unusual sight of the sheep with feathers and wings flying through the sky. This is just shear bliss!

meaningMnemonic: I'm putting all my shellfish on someone , hoping they'll win the race! This is a gamble and you're gambling. Hints Remember, shellfish used to be used as money. So if you're betting shellfish on someone, you're just gambling. And you probably won't get any of those shellfish back.
readingMnemonic: If you win this gamble you'll have enough shellfish to buy a brand new ca r ( か )! Hints If you go to any of those fancy (and not so fancy) gamble-places, they always have a car sitting in the middle of the room. Usually rotating, really slowly, to make you want it more, making you gamble more.

meaningMnemonic: Coming down with the rain is two spikes . They go right through two ghost s. Hints The ghosts are pinned to the ground by the spikes, unable to move.
readingMnemonic: You come across the ghost s, who are stabbed into the ground. "Please," they beg. "Please use that ray ( れい ) gun that's in that row ( りょう ) boat and end our suffering." Hints A ray gun, coincidentally, is the only thing that can kill a ghost, and there it lays, just out of reach. You'll have to be the one to pull the trigger of the ray gun. Do you pick up the ray gun out of the row boat to destroy the ghosts?

meaningMnemonic: Tsunami vs lifeguard . Who will win? After the water drains away, we find the lifeguard in the gutter . Hints To be fair, it's pretty obvious who would win. Nobody knows what that lifeguard was thinking.
readingMnemonic: In the gutter is a lifeguard, so Emperor こう いち decides to survey the damage. Hints "This lifeguard didn't believe in the power of kanji learning," こういち says to the press. "He was punished by the great Crabigator, who sent its tsunami as a warning for all." Hint: when you see the "lifeguard" radical, the reading is probably going to be こう .

meaningMnemonic: I protect my own animal s by going to hunt other animals... like wolves and cougars and such. Hints My animals can't protect themselves, that's why I hunt other animals instead.
readingMnemonic: I also do all my hunt s using a ca r ( か ). I just run those animals down with my car. Kind of cheating, but vroom vroom anyways. Hints Imagine hunting down animals in a car.

meaningMnemonic: If you've been to the moon in the past , you had to get the special stamp on your leg . Hints This leg stamp not only proved you went, but lets everyone around you know you've been to the moon before!
readingMnemonic: You've only met one other person with the same mark on their leg and it was Kyaku ( きゃく ) the customer. Kyaku visits many places all over the world, so it only makes sense that they've also been off-world too. Hints Picture Kyaku lifting up their pant leg and showing you all the stamps from all the different places they've been. There are even some planets on there!

meaningMnemonic: When the tsunami struck, it hit your tent full of beans . When you lost your tent of beans, you had a moment of lucidity . You don't need so much stuff, you can live without it! Hints Then you went back to being crazy. That moment of lucidity was only temporary, and you go back to stockpiling beans.
readingMnemonic: Your lucidity is clear to everyone because you wear a su it ( す ). Everyone knows that lucid people wear suits! Hints Imagine yourself wearing a sharp suit and being a model of lucidity.

meaningMnemonic: A dirt demon is just a lump . Just like a dust bunny is just a clump of dust. Hints Picture a lump of dirt. Is there a demon hiding under there? No. It's just a saying, ya nerd.
readingMnemonic: A lump of something is just a 固まり ( かたまり ) — the hardened thing itself. Hints 塊 is derived from 固まり , which is the noun form of 固まる (to be hardened). You know a lump is usually something that's compressed and hardened.

meaningMnemonic: The animal king ? He's just this guy who lives in the forest and thinks he's king of all the animals. He's a lunatic , though. Hints While we're speaking of animals, he's absolutely bat sh*t crazy.
readingMnemonic: You might see that crazy lunatic hanging around the outskirts of きょう と . He'll lurk near your trash cans and scream, "I AM THE ANIMAL KING!" and run away with some orange peels. Hints I think he maybe got too friendly with some raccoons and beavers and went crazy. Watch out for him if you live in きょうと , rabies is no joke.

meaningMnemonic: A woman who is a nurse should be called miss . Hints Compare this to a man who is a nurse. You should probably call him mister. That's why you know a woman who is a nurse is "miss."
readingMnemonic: "Call me Miss Joe ( じょう )," Joe says to you. Hints When you think of "miss," remember the time Joe asked you to call him "Miss Joe". He’s this big, ten foot tall guy, but now he suddenly wants you to call him Miss Joe. Well, we’re all for respecting everbody’s personal choices here, so we better get used to it.

meaningMnemonic: If your outfit is just a piece of fruit , then you are naked . Hints You're like one of those nudes in a Renaissance painting, strategically covering yourself with a bunch of grapes or a well-placed apple or something.
readingMnemonic: You know who else is often naked ? The ancient Egyptian god Ra ( ら ). Well, half-naked at least. Egypt is a hot country, so you can't really blame Ra for wanting to strip down. Hints Whatever you do, don't Google "Ra Egyptian god naked" to see how naked he actually got. There's no need to taint your browser history for the sake of kanji learning.

meaningMnemonic: An axe is sticking in the ground on top of a mountain . It's sticking into the very peak . Because why would you bother to stick your axe anywhere else on the mountain to prove you climbed it? Hints Picture that axe, jammed into the mountain's peak . The person who did that must have been really cool to get all the way up there.
readingMnemonic: You can't help but gawk ( がく ) at the peak . Somehow it looks even higher now. Hints Go ahead, imagine this peak with an axe in it and actually gawk a bit at how far you have to go to get that high.

meaningMnemonic: Below this canopy of tree s is a stone . Since it's the only stone here, you make sure to polish it. Hints It's a single, perfectly round stone under this canopy of trees. It didn't start this way, but thanks to all the polishing you did, it has become nice and smooth.
readingMnemonic: You polish the stone due to your meager ( みが ) lifestyle. Hints There's only this one stone under these trees, and polishing the stone is the only job here. Still, you don't get much from it, thus the meager life of polishing your stone.

meaningMnemonic: This building now has a cloud over it, creating shade . Hints This shade is really convenient right now, because it's been such a hot day. Ahh, the shade is so nice and cool.
readingMnemonic: The building that's getting this nice shade is the inn ( いん ) you're staying at. Hints Picture an inn with a cloud right above it right now. Look at the cloud-shaped shade that keeps everyone at the inn cool and sunburn-free.

meaningMnemonic: The moon table is a table that's made entirely of skin . You thought the table was made of moon, with all those pores and such, but when you look more closely, you realize it's skin. Disgusting, porous, skin. Hints Touch it and feel the "moon table." You know it's not made of moon. How ridiculous.
readingMnemonic: But, when you go to touch this "moon table" made of skin , you realize that it's harder ( はだ ) than you expected. Hints You'd think skin would be softer, but it's pretty hard. Much harder than you expected.

meaningMnemonic: The cloud floating above a demon has its soul in it. If you can manage to get through to the demon, to make it see that it doesn't have to be evil, it might remember who it is and return to the spirit it once was. Hints Right now, however, the demon is looming over you, and you can't see anything in the cloud above its head. It just looks mad, like it's gonna pummel you or eat you.
readingMnemonic: You shout out and beg its soul for help until, finally, you see the cloud take the shape of a con dor ( こん ). Aha! "You were a condor before you became a demon! Remember who you are and turn back!" Hints POOF! Now there's a condor spirit floating in front of you, crying. "Thank you, human. You've saved my soul!" it says, and float/flies off and disappears.

meaningMnemonic: The spear radical and the spear kanji are the same! Hints Spears are spears. It makes sense!
readingMnemonic: You take this spear and stab it into a cow. " MOO ( む )!" it cries. The cow bites the spear out of your hands and stabs you back. "MOO!" you scream. Hints How do you like it? Don't stab cows with spears, you monster.

meaningMnemonic: When your eye catches an omen , it's only natural that you will stare at it. Hints You don't see omens that often, so of course you're going to stare. We'll imagine what the omen is in the reading mnemonic.
readingMnemonic: As you stare at the omen, you see Mrs. Chou ( ちょう ) knocking down buildings, putting nails on the street, and making herself way longer than you ever thought possible. Oh, and there she is, destroying the world. Hints Whenever you see an omen (radical), remember that the omen will probably have Mrs. Chou in it!

meaningMnemonic: You feel like a stone that’s been renew ed. How do renewed stones feel? Stiff . Very stiff. Hints Think of a stone being renewed like it is having something like a spa day. Pedicure, manicure, the whole shebang. It’ll come out all stiff and hardened, cause that’s how good stones are.
readingMnemonic: You remember how you used to cure these stiff body times: your old friend こう いち would just massage them out for you. Hints If only you could ask こういち to give you massages again, but he's too busy for you, now (being emperor and all).

meaningMnemonic: The toe is early . I hate it when the toes show up early. Well, if the toes are going to show up this early, I guess it's best to put them on the table . Hints See all the toes lined up on the table . They are the ones who showed up early.
readingMnemonic: What do all the early toes on the table do while they're waiting until it's the right time? They just sit around on their table, talk ing ( たく ). Hints Imagine the toes talking to each other. "Hello Mr. Toe!" "Oh hello other Mr. Toe!"

meaningMnemonic: If there's a treasure chest , there's always a villain too. The villain is trying to get to the treasure chest before the hero of the story. Hints And the villain always gets to the treasure chest first, often via nefarious means. That villain is SO important when it comes to treasure chests.
readingMnemonic: The villain beat you all the way to きょう と to get this particular treasure chest. Hints Arrrg! If only you had been closer to きょうと ! Then you might have beaten this dastardly villain.

meaningMnemonic: A tsunami in the shape of a dragon flies off the cliff, then comes crashing down to the ground. This skinny tsunami of water flying down to the ground is a waterfall . Hints Can you see why a tsunami dragon (especially the Asian skinny snake-like kind) could be a waterfall? Try to imagine it.
readingMnemonic: Despite how cool a dragon waterfall is, to be honest it's also pretty tacky ( たき ). Hints Now imagine it being a bit tacky. Dragons are alright but... you just don't want to overdo it, you know?

meaningMnemonic: Something that is obsolete will end in extinction . Join in the calls for its abolition , elimination and extinction , whatever it is.
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

sentences.japanese: 核廃絶運動家たちは、核兵器を廃絶することは実現可能だと信じている。
sentences.english: The anti-nuclear movement believes that the abolition of nuclear weapons is feasible.

meaningMnemonic: いつ is "when" and 頃 is "about." Combine those together and you have " about when ?" or " how soon ?"
readingMnemonic: The reading is the same as the one you learned with the kanji, just rendaku'd.

sentences.japanese: トーフグはいつ頃Eブックマーケットに参入するつもりですか？
sentences.english: How soon will Tofugu enter into the e-book market?

meaningMnemonic: A warn bell is a bell that goes off when you need to be warned about something. This is usually an alarm bell or a fire bell .
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

sentences.japanese: 研究者たちは、どれだけ速く氷山が溶け出しているかについて警鐘を鳴らしている。
sentences.english: Researchers are sounding the alarm on how quickly the icebergs are melting.

meaningMnemonic: The year approximate is your approximate age . This is also an indirect way to refer to adolescence , and when people reach marriageable age !
readingMnemonic: The reading is the reading of the vocab version of 年 plus 頃 , put together. Note: You will also sometimes see this written partially in kana like 年ごろ .

sentences.japanese: あの子いつも一人だろう？彼、同じ年頃の友達がいないそうでどうも心配だ。
sentences.english: That kid's always alone, right? He doesn't seem to have friends his age so I can't help worrying about him.

sentences.japanese: 年頃の子が三人もいたら大変じゃない？
sentences.english: Isn't it hard to take care of three adolescent kids?

sentences.japanese: うちの娘はもう年ごろなのに、キャリアに集中したいと言っていて、全然その気がないらしいのよ。
sentences.english: My daughter has become old enough to get married, but seems to have absolutely no desire to do so, saying that she'd rather focus on her career.

meaningMnemonic: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. When used as a suffix, it means approximate time and around (as in "around 3:00").
readingMnemonic: The reading is the same as what you learned with the kanji. Bear in mind that it's pronounced ころ when it's a noun, but it's usually ごろ when it's a suffix, though some people say ころ in both cases.

sentences.japanese: じゃあ、7時頃また電話しますよ。
sentences.english: Well, I'll call you again around 7 o'clock.

sentences.japanese: あの頃、俺は人気者だったんだよ。
sentences.english: I was popular back then.

sentences.japanese: 今日のお昼の三時頃、この公園でツキノワグマが目撃されました。
sentences.english: Around three o’clock this afternoon, a moon bear was seen in this park.

sentences.japanese: 私の履歴書には空白期間があります。というのも、その頃はワニカニばかりやっていたからです。その期間の生活はほぼワニカニ中心で、私はひたすらレベル60を目指していました。
sentences.english: My résumé has a gap in it. That's because I spent that period almost entirely focused on WaniKani. My daily life basically revolved around reviews, and I was determined to reach level 60.

meaningMnemonic: A villain who is bad is the most atrocious and fiendish villain of them all.
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

sentences.japanese: 誰もが、その凶悪犯が刑務所で大人しく刑期を務めるのは無理だろうと思っていました。
sentences.english: Everyone believed that the atrocious criminal would not fare well in prison.

meaningMnemonic: A thin bacteria is... well... a bacteria . I guess all bacteria are really thin. So thin you can't see them with your naked eye, in fact.
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You've learned them already, so you should be able to read this on your own!

sentences.japanese: 最近真剣に細菌について勉強をし始めました。
sentences.english: Recently, I started seriously studying bacteria.

meaningMnemonic: Remember how 趣味 means "hobby"? Well, if you have bad hobbies, it probably means you have bad taste . 悪趣味 is often used to describe something that lacks sophistication or sensitivity, like tacky shoes and offensive jokes, as well as someone with that kind of taste.
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

sentences.japanese: 母は、父が悪趣味な人形を集めることを禁止しました。
sentences.english: My mom forbade my dad from collecting tasteless dolls.

meaningMnemonic: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. 鐘 usually refers to larger, open-ended bell s of the sort you might find in a church's bell tower or a Buddhist temple.
readingMnemonic: Seeing the bell , you decide you need to ring it. You take your cane ( かね ) and hit the bell as hard as you can, making it chime.

sentences.japanese: 正午になると鐘が12回鳴るんです。
sentences.english: The bell rings twelve times at noon.

sentences.japanese: 鐘の音を聞くと心が落ち着きます。
sentences.english: Hearing the bell calms my mind.

sentences.japanese: 私が旅行者だと言うと、男は鐘の形をしたお守りの値段を明らかにつり上げたが、何だかそいつに悪い気がして、そのまま何も言わずに言われた通りの値段を払ったんだよ。
sentences.english: When I told him I was a tourist, he blatantly raised the price of the bell-shaped charm, but I felt a little sorry for him, so I held my tongue and paid the price he told me anyway.

meaningMnemonic: The noun version of gamble is gambling or betting or a gamble or a bet . Whatever you do, put it all on black 13. Trust me.
readingMnemonic: The reading comes from the reading you learned with the kanji.

sentences.japanese: あいつとの賭けに勝ったよ。
sentences.english: I won a bet against him.

meaningMnemonic: A small boat is a boat or small craft . If something is a "big boat" it's better to call it a "ship" I think, which is why this is just a boat .
readingMnemonic: The readings are all ones you've seen before. 小 uses its こ reading, so just think of this like a "child boat." This makes sense because it's small. Watch out for the rendaku.

sentences.japanese: 太平洋上には小舟がひしめきあっていた。
sentences.english: The Pacific Ocean was filled with little boats.

meaningMnemonic: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. Note that this word isn't usually used by itself (that would be 船 ). It's usually attached to things that are boat-related, but I wanted you to learn it individually so you can use it that way.
readingMnemonic: The reading is the same as what you learned with the kanji. Also the same as 船 .

sentences.japanese: いさり舟をハンマーで叩いて破壊した。
sentences.english: I destroyed the fishing boat with a hammer.

meaningMnemonic: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well.
readingMnemonic: The reading is the same as the one you learned with the kanji.

sentences.japanese: 靴下を裏返しに履いちゃうと、嫁が怒ってうるさいんだわ。
sentences.english: My wife gets upset with me whenever I wear my socks inside out.

sentences.english: My wife never turns off the light. I don't think she even knows there's a switch.

meaningMnemonic: An electricity table is a calculator . Why is this? You can think about it in a couple of different ways. Maybe in the past, a calculator (aka abacus) would take up a whole table, making this "electric" version a calculator. Or, maybe it can be used to solve tables. Wrong kind of table, but should help you to remember the meaning of this word.
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

sentences.english: Please stop drumming on the calculator. You’re driving me crazy!

meaningMnemonic: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well.

sentences.japanese: うちの会社は暦通りの営業になります。
sentences.english: Our company’s business days follow the regular calendar.

meaningMnemonic: A ghost garden is where many ghosts are harvested and where many ghosts grow. This is a cemetery .
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

sentences.english: My family took our puppy to a pet cemetery.

meaningMnemonic: The noun version of cloudy is cloudy weather or cloudiness . In some cases, this can also refer to the type of fog you'd find on a window or your glasses. Despite being a noun in Japanese, you'll actually see this translated as the adjective "cloudy" in English a lot. Don't let that fool you, though, it still behaves as a noun in Japanese! sentences.english: to marry into a family of farmers

sentences.english: to marry into a family living in Niigata

sentences.english: to marry into the Sakurai family

sentences.japanese: 嫁ぎたての頃は、息子の嫁はかまととぶっていました。
sentences.english: Around the time they got married, my son’s wife pretended she was a prude.

meaningMnemonic: Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means polish and the verb vocab version is to polish or, strangely specifically (and we'll learn an even more specific word for this later) to brush your teeth .
readingMnemonic: The reading is the same as the one you learned with the kanji.

sentences.japanese: 何で切れた電球なんか磨いてるの？
sentences.english: Why are you polishing a light bulb that’s already burnt out?

meaningMnemonic: Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means rub and this verb means to rub or to scrub .
readingMnemonic: If you're going to rub me like that, I'm going to sue ( す ) you. It's making me very uncomfortable. The cos t  ( こす ) of your rubbing actions will be high. So this word has two readings and both mean “to rub.” But you usually use する for a single action, such as lighting a match or grazing your knee, while こする means doing it repeatedly, like when you’re cleaning or polishing something.

sentences.japanese: 花粉症で目を擦ってたら、片方のコンタクトレンズが破けました。
sentences.english: I was rubbing my eyes because of my allergies and one of my contact lenses was torn.

meaningMnemonic: Everything we're doing is to serve you, you know. This verb is a bit archaic and therefore has a formal feel to it. It's used to talk about serving emperors, kings, and gods, among others.
readingMnemonic: To serve you well, we've gotten ourselves two ca rs ( つか ). If one breaks down, we can still serve you with the other car.

sentences.japanese: この家に仕える使用人は、とても礼儀が正しい。
sentences.english: The servants who serve in this house are very polite.

sentences.japanese: その女性は、明治天皇に仕えていた女官のようです。
sentences.english: The woman seemed to be a female official in the service of the Meiji Emperor.

sentences.japanese: はじめまして。今日から神に仕えることになった天使です。
sentences.english: Nice to meet you. I'm an angel who started serving God today.

meaningMnemonic: Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means stare and the verb vocab version is to stare at (or to look at in a very staringish way).
readingMnemonic: To learn the reading, just think about how you're looking at something for a lonnnnng time if you're staring at it. In Japanese the word "long" is 長い , and guess what the reading of the kanji part is? It's なが , just like なが める 's kanji-part reading.

sentences.japanese: うちの甥っ子は新幹線を見るのが好きで、一日中眺めていることもできます。
sentences.english: My nephew likes watching the Shinkansen so much that he can stare at it all day long.

sentences.japanese: 僕は寝床でスマホを眺めながら、終わりのない情報の波に流されていた。
sentences.english: Looking at my phone in bed, I was carried along on an endless tide of information.

meaningMnemonic: You know that 裂く is "to tear" or "to rip up." So, if you're trying to tear or rip up something, and you're pull ing it at the same time, you are going to tear up that thing, or more accurately perhaps to tear off something, since you're pulling.
readingMnemonic: The reading comes from 引く and 裂く .

sentences.japanese: あのカップルの仲をうまく引き裂く事ができたら、お知らせ致します。
sentences.english: I’ll let you know if I succeed in splitting up the couple.

meaningMnemonic: As usual, you can guess this is a verb thanks to the う sound on the end. The kanji means frustration , and unfortunately frustration tends to torment people. This verb is pretty advanced, but still useful to know!
readingMnemonic: We all know it's not okay to to torment each other. So how about we all sign a ( さいな ) contract saying that we'll never torment anyone ever again?

sentences.japanese: 無力感に苛まれてるんよ。
sentences.english: I'm tormented by feelings of helplessness.

sentences.japanese: うだるような暑さが私達を苛む。
sentences.english: The sweltering heat torments us.

sentences.japanese: 被害者はまた何か悪いことが起こるのではないかという不安に苛まれていました。
sentences.english: The victims were tormented by the anxiety that something else bad would happen.

meaningMnemonic: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well.
readingMnemonic: The reading is the same as the one you learned with the kanji.

sentences.japanese: 一位のチームには、賞品として滝修行が授与されます。
sentences.english: The top team will be awarded with a prize of doing aesthetic waterfall meditation.

meaningMnemonic: The damp earth is where water seems to congregate, but not so much that there's a lake or ocean or anything like that. Just damp. This is a wetlands .
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

sentences.japanese: 確か、北海道には湿地が多いんだよね？
sentences.english: If I am not mistaken, there are a lot of wetlands in Hokkaido, right?

meaningMnemonic: A 包み is a bundle or package , and 紙 is paper . What paper goes around bundles and packages? That would be wrapping paper .
readingMnemonic: The reading is 包み and 紙 combined together. Be careful of rendaku.

sentences.japanese: この包み紙には点字が施してあるわ。
sentences.english: There is braille on this wrapping paper.
